saints.name: St. Josephine Bakhita
saints.title: Virgin
saints.shortBlurb: A Sudanese girl seized into slavery who found her true freedom in Christ and became a beloved Canossian sister in Italy…
biography: Born about 1869 at Olgossa in Darfur in the Sudan, she was kidnapped as a child by slave-traders and sold in the markets of El Obeid and Khartoum, passing from master to master, some of them cruel. Her captors named her Bakhita, 'the fortunate one'; her own name she no longer remembered.

In 1883 she was bought by Callisto Legnani, the Italian consul at Khartoum, who brought her to Italy in 1885. Given to the Michieli family of Venice as nurse to their daughter, she came to know the faith through the Canossian sisters, and on 9 January 1890 was baptized with the name Josephine.

When her mistress tried to take her back to Africa, an Italian court declared her free. She entered the Canossian Daughters of Charity in 1893, made her vows in 1896, and for some fifty years served at Schio as cook, sacristan, and portress, calling God 'the Master.'

She died at Schio on 8 February 1947 and was canonized in 2000 by Pope John Paul II. Herself once bought and sold, she is patron of the Sudan and of victims of human trafficking, and her feast is a day of prayer against that trade.
saints.knownFor: Her witness of forgiveness and faith after a childhood in slavery.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of St. Josephine Bakhita (vatican.va)
